Futures prices drift on news and with limited liquidity; the path shows staleness and information arrival.

Realized frequency by rung across seasons is the only calibration source for rare season-level events.
MVP, All-NBA, DPOY and Clutch markets can flip from near-certain to impossible on one game, so the ledger is the first gate for every candidate price.
The candidate field and the named statistic differ per series, so a single production metric misranks Sixth Man, Clutch and MIP contenders.
Coach of the Year, Executive of the Year and MIP prices should key off surprise rather than wins; the existing catalog has no baseline for it.
Rung markets on 1st/2nd/3rd team are cumulative on the same ranking and need an enforced consistent ladder, which the market's independent quotes may violate.
Pick-slot and team-to-draft markets settle on ownership as much as on prospect choice, and traded protections create incentives that move standings.
Draft slot markets on picks 1-10 are priced as separate coins; the Plackett-Luce structure enforces that one prospect fills one slot.
Monthly series are decided in a fixed short window where a schedule difference of three games matters.
Carries the dominant 50% fan component and slot arithmetic that the media-ballot stage omits, which is the mechanism behind the live starters and All-Stars series.
Reserves are decided by a different electorate than starters and by a different rule, and the roster markets need both.
Gives the narrative and voter-fatigue effects an observable form for MVP, DPOY, ROY and similar awards.
Captures the All-Star voting calendar, captains and event participation that fix when fan-vote returns and roster announcements arrive; context for the starter and reserve inputs.
Series and Cup MVP markets need P(team wins the series or title) as the first factor.
Series length and winner per round feed the series-MVP first factor and the number of games a candidate accumulates.
Second factor of every series MVP market: P(player chosen | his team wins), driven by series scoring share and best-player status.
Nominee/panel awards (Social Justice Champion, Teammate, Sportsmanship, series MVPs) and the $1/N co-winner payout need a nominee-set and co-winner model.
KXNBALOTTERYODDS, KXNBATOPPICK and KXNBATOP3 settle on the lottery draw, which is the published odds table applied to the final pre-lottery ranks.
KXNBAHALLOFFAME needs P(inductee) through a two-stage committee election that no ballot, draft or All-Star input describes.
Prices all draft range, matchup, count and comparison markets from one coherent order.
Turns MVP/All-NBA eligibility from a hard ledger into ledger plus a dated appeal branch, which moved 2025-26 award prices.
The 16/8 minimum with Commissioner additions is a selection stage the vote composite cannot produce.
KXNBAHUSTLE is settled by a tracked-stat formula; without this index the series has no driver.
Cup MVP depends on which team survives the group tiebreaks and the knockout games (higher seed hosts through the semifinal; neutral final).
65-game rule (20+ minutes in 63) gates MVP, DPOY, MIP, All-NBA and All-Defensive; ROY, Sixth Man, All-Rookie and the draft are exempt.

interactions.hypothesis: Voters reward production attached to team success, so model vote share with an interaction between individual metrics and team win percentage.
Eligibility is a hard gate: a player on the games-played bubble has a bimodal outcome.
Narrative shifts in the final weeks can overcome small metric gaps; use ladder trackers as a signal with caution.
Pre-draft trades and workout news create large consensus changes in the final days.

Voters treat team success as a gate: production wins only when the team is a top-two seed, and below that seed the same production sees a sharp discount, especially for MVP and DPOY; the effect is much smaller for ROY and MIP.
At zero slack a single missed game removes a candidate completely, so the probability is a step in games remaining rather than a smooth penalty; players with high slack are insulated.

Similar candidates split ballot ranks: two centres with equal metrics both fall relative to a lone candidate with the same metrics, and a surplus of strong forwards lowers P(third team) for a marginal one.

Coach of the Year rewards positive surprise but saturates once a team is already a top seed, because a title favourite cannot overperform much; a mid-seed team with a large surprise beats a top seed with a small one.

Slot probabilities for prospects depend on who holds the pick: a team with a veteran roster, a rebuilding team and a team trading the pick pick differently, so P(prospect at slot k) is conditional on the holder.

A series MVP needs both his team to win and the panel to pick him, so a star on a modest favourite can be worth less than the second option on a heavy favourite; the product, not either factor, ranks candidates, and both update after every game.

awards_draft.label: NBA awards, All-NBA selections and draft
awards_draft.mechanism: Awards and selections are results of voting or formula: production and advanced metrics, team success, games played (the 65-game rule with its Extraordinary Circumstances appeal for MVP, DPOY, MIP, All-NBA and All-Defensive) and narrative interact; All-NBA ballots are positionless; All-Star starters and reserves are positionless with a nationality minimum; the Hustle Award is a tracked-stat formula. Draft outcomes depend on lottery order, consensus rankings and trade/workout news. Mostly slow-moving until late-season/draft-week information arrives.
awards_draft.target: Award winner, All-NBA selections and draft position/outcomes

interactions.hypothesis: Minutes volatility induces positive covariance between components, widening the tails of the combo relative to independent sums.
For creators, scoring and assist usage trade off; combo variance can be smaller than the sum of single-stat variances.
Combo right tail (high rung) depends on blowout probability more than the mean; model with scenario mixture.
With a big out, a wing's rebounds can rise while scoring is unchanged; component-level updates are not uniform.

Expected opportunities are the product of minutes and per-minute volume, but the usage rate itself is lower in garbage minutes, so the product within the blowout regime is much smaller than average minutes times average usage.

With the primary creator off court, points and assists move in opposite directions for the scorer-passer while points and rebounds move together for a big, so the covariance sign by component pair flips with the lineup.
Past a expected margin of about 10 points the probability of a truncated-minutes game rises steeply, creating a regime switch in the upper rungs while the lower rungs barely move.

A questionable teammate's resolution changes the player's usage and assists, and since the protected clause treats the player's own exit separately, the sequence of reports matters: the teammate's status effect is conditional on the player's status being active.

A protected contract voids a first-half exit, so P(Yes | not void) is a conditional on survival to the second half, shifting probability up for high-hazard players relative to the unprotected equivalent.

combo_props.label: NBA combo props (PRA, PR, PA, RA)
combo_props.mechanism: A combo is a sum of correlated components; the mean is the sum of marginal means, while the variance depends on within-game covariance (minutes positive, role tradeoffs negative). Mispricing arises when a market prices combos as independent sums of the component lines, or when component prices update at different speeds after news. All single-stat drivers apply, with minutes and game script as common factors that dominate the tails.
combo_props.target: Combined player points+rebounds+assists (or subset) over a strike

Winning the tip raises the team's first-score probability only by the chain factor, and the gain shrinks when the opponent's opening conversion is high because the loser gets the next possession quickly; the effect is conditional on the opponent's pB.
A newly promoted starter inherits the scripted plays of the old slot only partially; the probability that he takes the first shot is conditional on the slot and on the game-count of the new five.

Make probability of the opening shot is shot-type base rate times the opponent's allowed rate in that zone; a rim opener against a drop coverage that concedes mid-range is lower than the base rim rate.

When one starter is out, scripted shots reallocate to the remaining one or two creators and the first-basket probabilities of the five are negatively correlated, so a single player's share cannot rise without reducing others.

first_basket.label: NBA first basket scorer / first team to score
first_basket.mechanism: P(player scores first) = P(team scores first) x P(player is the scorer | team's first basket). Tip and opening-set plays determine possession; first-shot allocation is designed (ATO/opening play) and concentrated in the starters; make probability on the first shot is near league average. Conditional on starters it is mainly a usage and set-play problem with small samples. Player must start; rules cover postponement and tip ordering.
first_basket.target: Which player scores the first basket (or team scores first) of the game

interactions.hypothesis: Value of a questionable star is asymmetric: a mixture over play/no-play must be priced, and the quote may reflect one branch.
Back-to-back effect operates mainly through star rest; fit the direct effect after controlling for availability.
A defense with lucky opponent 3P% allowed is overrated in raw defensive rating; regress toward shot-quality allowed.
Large spreads change margin variance; at -12 and beyond cover probability depends on late bench minutes.
Teams with seeding locked and stars resting create unusually uncertain rosters.

A questionable star creates a two-point mixture whose mean differs by several points, so the market price may match only one branch; with two questionable players the branches multiply and the cost is non-additive, so the mixture cannot be reduced to an expected rating.
The back-to-back effect is mostly a star-rest effect; conditional on all stars playing, the direct fatigue effect on margin is small (around a point) and larger for older rosters.

Cover probability at a given spread depends on mean/sd, and sd rises with pace and total while the mean is set by ratings, so a fast game with a large favourite covers a wide spread less often than a slow game with the same mean.
Rating correction for hot three-point shooting is proportional to the team's three-point attempt rate: a team with 45% of shots from three has more luck variance to remove than one with 30%.

In a series, defensive scheme adjustments after game 2-3 reduce the offence's advantage, so a regular-season matchup edge decays across games; the effect is regime-dependent on whether the coach changes the coverage.

game_moneyline_spread.label: NBA game winner and point-spread markets
game_moneyline_spread.mechanism: Margin = sum over possessions of efficiency differences, shifted by home court, rest and, most importantly, who plays. Sharp closing lines are efficient on average, so model value comes from (1) availability changes between the injury-report vintage priced by Kalshi and the true scenario mixture, (2) regression of luck-contaminated ratings (3P%, close games), (3) variance shape (margin sd grows with spread; OT mass), and (4) Kalshi-specific stale quotes and rung inconsistencies in spread ladders.
game_moneyline_spread.target: Team wins outright or covers a stated spread over the full game (OT included per rules text)

interactions.hypothesis: A rested starter becomes a bench player in the market's definition, mechanically raising bench points if the scorer plays.

The tie probability is the Gaussian pmf at zero, which decays like exp(-mu^2/(2 sigma^2)); the loss from a 4-point expected margin to a 10-point expected margin is far larger than from 0 to 4, so the effect of expected margin on P(OT) is convex-then-flat in the tail.

The excess tie mass is conditional on the game being within three points with under 30 seconds left and on the trailing coach's policy; if the leading team intentionally fouls, ties become less likely than by smooth density.

When the top scorer is promoted into the starting five by an absence, he leaves the bench count and bench points drop by his share; when a returning star plays off the bench on a restriction, bench points rise by his minutes times his rate, a discrete jump.

Bench minutes rise with blowout probability but saturate once starters sit entirely, around 150-170 minutes; beyond that extra blowout size adds nothing, while within the competitive range additional margin adds quickly.

The two teams' counts rise and fall together with pace, so a pace shock moves both and leaves the difference nearly unchanged; the difference's sd is smaller than independent counts would give, and the covariance is higher in games with competitive scores.

The trailing team raises its three-point attempt share late in lopsided games while the leader slows down, so the expected made-threes difference shrinks toward zero (or flips) in blowout scripts even when the favourite is the higher-volume team; this cuts the favourite's edge in KXNBAH2HTEAM3PT.

A team's bench total jumps once the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early in the fourth quarter, because the starters' remaining minutes convert to reserve minutes for both sides, and a pregame starter scratch moves one reserve out of the bench pool; the level and the variance of KXNBABENCHPTS therefore switch between a normal-rotation regime and a blowout regime, and a scratch shifts the whole distribution rather than its tail.

game_overtime_and_team_events.label: NBA overtime, bench points and team-stat head-to-head
game_overtime_and_team_events.mechanism: Overtime requires a regulation tie: probability follows the margin density at zero (about 5-6% unconditional), higher in tight spreads and slightly higher for slower games, and independent of spread outside narrow ranges. Bench-points markets scale with starter minutes, bench quality and blowout probability; the definition of bench (non-starters) interacts with lineup changes. Team-stat head-to-heads compare two correlated counts where pace correlation shrinks variance.
game_overtime_and_team_events.target: Game goes to overtime; bench points over a strike (entity unresolved for KXNBABENCHPTS, a head-to-head for KXNBAH2HBENCHPTS); team A stat vs team B stat

interactions.hypothesis: Totals fall more than additive when two slow, strong-defense teams meet because tempo is controlled by the slower team.
Missing a primary ball handler can slow pace while reducing efficiency; missing a rim protector can raise efficiency but not pace.
Offense inflated by recent hot 3P% overstates expected scoring; the correction is larger for teams with high 3PA.
Crew effect is concentrated in high-FTA offenses and in games with big-man foul trouble.
If OT is included, add expected OT points weighted by tie probability; wording must be matched per market.

Total equals possessions times combined points per possession, so a fast game between two efficient offences is multiplicatively larger than the sum of separate pace and efficiency effects; the cross term is about 1.5-2 points when both factors are one sd above average.

Missing a primary ball handler lowers pace and efficiency (total falls), while missing a rim protector raises opponent efficiency without changing pace (total rises); the sign depends on the missing role.

Crew whistle tendency matters most for teams that live at the line: a high-foul crew adds free-throw points proportional to both teams' free-throw rate, so the crew effect on total is larger when both offences draw many fouls.

A hot three-point streak is more likely to be luck for a high-3PA team (larger noise per game), so regression is heavier for those teams and the variance load is also larger; direction: shrink recent offence more when volume is high.

Close games produce both late-fouling free-throw points and OT, so the extra points are positively correlated within the same games; the upper tail of the total is generated by close games more than by high-pace blowouts.

game_total.label: NBA full-game total points
game_total.mechanism: Total = possessions x combined points per possession. Possessions depend on both teams' pace and lineups; efficiency on opponent-adjusted offense/defense, shot-making luck and free-throw volume. Late-game fouling and OT add tail mass; injuries to ball handlers and scorers shift both pace and efficiency. The sharp total is usually efficient, so value is in injury-scenario mixtures, luck regression and rung-level inconsistencies.
game_total.target: Combined points over a half-point strike (OT included per rules text)

A band probability is a CDF difference (mu-b)/sigma, so errors in sigma and in mu multiply: when the mean is near a band's centre, sigma matters more than mu, but for a band two sds away mu matters more.

Once the lead exceeds about 15 with under six minutes left the starters leave and the margin drifts rather than grows; the effect of an extra point of lead on the final margin falls from about one to about 0.5 beyond the threshold.
The drift after the pull depends on the second-unit gap: a leading team with the stronger bench keeps its lead, otherwise it shrinks; the sign is conditional on the gap.

In the regime where regulation ties (3-6% of games) the final margin follows the folded OT density, which is concentrated in 1-8; the lowest bands are a mixture of regulation and OT regimes and the mixture weight falls with spread.
In a faster game there are more possessions in the final two minutes, so the late-foul sequences take more time and add margins in 4-8 points; pmf spikes become less pronounced as pace rises.

game_win_margin.label: NBA winning-margin buckets
game_win_margin.mechanism: Bucketed margin outcomes are a discretization of the margin distribution: mean from the availability-adjusted spread, shape from empirical residual (sd 11-12, fatter tails for lopsided matchups), plus OT effect that collapses ties to a 1-3 point margin. Bucket edges and inclusivity are rules-driven. Value exists where buckets are priced as independent while they must sum to a coherent distribution.
game_win_margin.target: Winning team and margin bucket (e.g. 1-5, 6-10, 11-15, 16+) at settlement including OT per rules

interactions.hypothesis: A reported trade is only likely to complete if matching rules and deadlines allow; rumor probability should be conditioned on feasibility.
Coach changes cluster after underperformance vs expectation and at schedule breaks.
The official-announcement wording decides the effective event time; leaks before the announcement do not settle the market.

A top-tier report that an agreement is signed multiplies with the remaining approval pipeline probability; a reliable report at the agreed stage still leaves the approval and timing risk, so the market should not jump to one.

Trade probability collapses after the deadline and spikes in the days before it, so the hazard is convex in days to deadline; feasibility constraints bind most tightly in the last week when salary-matching is tested.

A franchise star is traded mostly when his team turns seller: the KXNBATRADE hazard stays near its floor while the team is near or above expectation and rises steeply once the team falls clearly below it before the deadline, more so after a front-office change; rumours about a star on a contender convert rarely whatever their volume.

The same news item resolves differently under different wordings: an agreement in principle satisfies an announcement market but not a Board-award or league-processing market, so one report moves the series in opposite directions.

A retirement announcement clusters after the season ends and before free agency, so the player's age hazard is conditional on being in that period; before the season's end the hazard is lower regardless of age.

Pick trades agreed on draft night count only if officially processed before the window end; deals with salaried players are processed only after the July moratorium, so the agreed-trade hazard is truncated by a hard date for one deal type and not the other.

Before leaks the pairing probability comes from the selection model's TV-appeal features; once a tier-one reporter leaks the Christmas or opening slate, probability jumps to near certainty regardless of features, so the model applies only in the pre-leak regime.

Realignment probability is near zero unless the expansion vote passes; once two Western cities are awarded, one Western incumbent must move East to make 16/16, so KXNBAJOINCONF jumps from a residual to a high conditional probability exactly at the final expansion vote.

Priors come from base rates of similar events by team and timing; the main edge is the correct interpretation of reporter reliability and the settlement wording.

interactions.hypothesis: Favorite cover plus star over has negative dependence via minutes; underdog cover plus star over positive.

One injury news item is a common shock to all legs; correlated repricing creates arbitrage vs independent pricing.

The favourite-cover and star-over pair (for stars of either team) becomes negatively dependent through minutes only when the projected |expected margin| passes about 6-8 points, since starters of both teams sit only in lopsided games; below the threshold the two are close to independent.
A single pace shock lifts the game total and every player's counting stats, so total-over with two player overs has a high joint probability beyond the product; loadings determine how much.

When a major teammate is ruled out, allocation shifts and the previously negative dependence between two remaining teammates' overs can turn less negative because both gain usage; the sign is conditional on the injury scenario.

The same injury news produces a void leg (player inactive) or a live leg with a minute limit; the combo rule on void legs switches the payoff structure, so the effective probability is regime-dependent.

The correlation between margin and total is close to zero overall but positive for slow-paced underdog games and negative for fast-paced favourite runaways, so the joint is not a simple bivariate normal.

The pair's value is the product of the two title probabilities only while both teams are alive; once the NBA leg's team advances a round the pair's value rises proportionally, and any elimination is absorbing, so value moves as a function of the round reached in both leagues.

A late scratch on one leg moves only that leg's win probability, but because the pack is a product, a drop from 0.65 to 0.50 on one leg cuts the 3-leg joint by 23% relative; status uncertainty on several legs compounds, so the joint's uncertainty band is much wider than any single leg's.

parlay_combo.label: NBA parlay / multi-leg combination markets
parlay_combo.mechanism: A joint event across legs whose dependence matters: side and total correlate through team scoring, side and player props through blowout minutes, and several props of the same player through minutes. A missing finisher cuts conversion while potential assists stay constant, a missing creator raises the player's potential assists, so the direction of the absence effect on assists depends on the absent player's role; a single dummy averages opposite effects to zero.
A lead guard on a heavy favourite loses late minutes, which removes the upper rungs; effect appears beyond a expected margin threshold near 8-10 and concentrates in the 9+ assist rungs.

player_assists.label: NBA player assists over/under ladder

Teammate absences change both factors in opposite directions depending on whether the absent player is a creator or a finisher. Blowouts truncate minutes; official-scorer credit adds noise.
player_assists.target: Player assists over an integer strike (2+ to 12+)

KXNBACOMPETE needs a signing and then a regular-season second on court, so P(Yes) sums over signing dates of the signing hazard times the probability the coach uses him in one of the games left; a mid-season injury-replacement signing nearly always plays, while a late buyout-market signing onto a deep contender may sit for weeks, so the second factor is low exactly when the first spikes.

The preseason starter signal matters only for contested spots; for an incumbent star the signal is weak but for a battle between two players the last preseason starts are decisive, so the information value is conditional on the competition.

Team rest decisions are shared, so two stars tend to sit together on back-to-backs; the joint availability has a covariance beyond independence, reducing co-appearance relative to the product for a pair on the same team with a rest-heavy coach.

A reported destination from a reliable source moves probability only if the feasibility screen passes; a rumor to an infeasible team (no cap room, no matching assets) has probability near zero regardless of source credibility.

A late-playoff return window pays only if the team is still playing when the player is cleared, so the recovery probability is multiplied by team survival game by game; a player with a 70% chance of being ready by the conference finals is worth much less on a team that is an underdog to get there.

interactions.hypothesis: The tail beyond 5 threes or 35 points depends on rare high-minutes high-variance outcomes; mixture modeling matters.
Tail probability is convex in both attempts and make rate; over-shrinking or under-shrinking changes expected payout materially.
The payout table must be parsed per series; convexity changes which part of the distribution drives the expected payout.

The top bands are reached when a heavy-minutes game coincides with hot shooting, and since both are rare, their joint probability determines the tail; the product of marginal tail probabilities underestimates it when close games also increase attempts.

The count of made threes is attempts times make rate, so the tail is convex in both; over-shrinking the make rate shrinks the tail multiplicatively while a high-attempt shooter's tail is more sensitive to the rate.

Under a convex payout, expected value is more than the payout at the mean (Jensen), so overdispersion raises value and an underestimate of variance understates it; the effect is larger the steeper the schedule.

In a blowout the starter's minutes drop and the count falls to low bands; since the payout is convex, losing the upper tail costs more than the shift of the mean, and the effect appears beyond a expected margin threshold of about 10 points.

Free-throw trips add odd points that move outcomes between 2-point bands; for a player with high FTA the parity of the composite matters more than for a pure jump shooter, so the band mass is conditional on FT mix.

The distribution is a mixture over minutes scenarios with overdispersed attempts and make rates. Settlement tables are in rules_primary and differ by series. Value arises where the market schedule over- or under-weights extreme counts relative to a calibrated tail model.
player_escalator_payout.target: Expected payout of a single-game player stat under a convex payout schedule (e.g. points in 2-point bands, 0-10+ threes)

interactions.hypothesis: Attempt volume is crew-dependent, with biggest effect on rim-attacking guards and bigs.
Leading-team ball handlers gain FTA in close games; in blowouts the pattern vanishes.
Low-FT% bigs have high variance outcomes with attempts; Hack-a-style fouls raise attempts when game is close.

Crew whistle scales shooting-foul rates, and attempts scale with the player's rim and post volume, so the crew effect is multiplicative with exposure: a rim attacker gains more from a high-foul crew than a spot-up shooter.
Hack-a policies are triggered when a player's free-throw percentage is below about 60% and the game is within a possession or two; outside that state the target probability is near zero.

The variance of makes depends on both attempts and rate: for a 60% shooter the binomial variance per attempt is larger than for an 85% shooter, so high-volume poor shooters have a wider count distribution than high-volume good shooters with the same mean.

The bonus effect applies in the minutes after the opponent reaches five team fouls in the period, so attempts depend on when in the quarter the player is on court; a player resting in late quarters misses the bonus window.

In a close game the last minutes produce many free throws for ball handlers, while in a blowout those minutes are played by bench players and no intentional fouls occur; the regime depends on the margin at 5:00 left.

The variance of a difference is var_A + var_B minus twice the covariance, so a positive correlation between opposing players narrows the distribution and raises tie probability, while a negative correlation between teammates widens it; the pair type reverses the effect of the same marginals.

A series total is a sum over a random number of games, so a longer series disproportionately raises the upper tail; mean games enter linearly but sd of the total depends on the variance of game counts, which is larger for even matchups than for mismatches.

If a star is lost for the rest of a series his total stops accumulating and the head-to-head may void; the probability of staying healthy across games declines multiplicatively with persistence, creating a threshold-like drop in total after the first injury.
The position-based allowance matters only if the assigned defender follows the position; when a coach assigns a wing stopper to a guard the position average is wrong, so the assignment overrides it.

A top pick plays a fraction of Summer League games with capped minutes, while a veteran plays all games with full minutes, so stat accumulation is a regime-dependent mixture that depends on the draft-slot bucket.

interactions.hypothesis: Double-double probability has a steep threshold in minutes; blowout risk reduces probability disproportionately.
A big who creates (high assists) has TD probability driven by both opportunity counts; shooters rarely get a third category.
Teammate absences can push a player over a threshold; historical rates in similar absence scenarios beat season averages.

DD probability is nearly flat above ~34 minutes and falls steeply below ~26, so a blowout that trims a starter from 35 to 28 minutes costs far more than one trimming 38 to 33; the effect is largest for players whose second category is marginal (rebounds around 8).

A center's rebound chances are shared with the other big only when both are on the floor, so the same rebound pool yields different counts depending on the fraction of minutes spent paired versus alone; direction is positive for the survivor when the co-big is out.

A fast game raises misses, possessions and assist chances together, which fattens the joint upper tail of rebounds and points more than the marginals alone; this correlates the two required components of a pts+reb DD and increases conjunction probability beyond the product of marginals.

A designated player is in one of two regimes: normal-load or limited/returning; in the latter the exit hazard and minute cap shift probability mass to very short appearances which settle NO, and the voiding rule does not help.

Inside the blowout branch, a player at 9 in a category late is more likely than his per-minute rate implies to finish, because teammates funnel the last opportunity; this partially offsets the minutes loss, in the direction opposite to the naive blowout penalty.

The playoff triple-double probability compounds a per-game rate over a random number of games: doubling expected games less than doubles P(YES) for high-rate creators, but nearly doubles it for occasional triple-double players, so advancement matters most for the long shots.

player_milestones.label: NBA double-double / triple-double
player_milestones.mechanism: Binary conjunction of count thresholds; probability depends on the joint distribution of points, rebounds and assists, each of which depends on minutes and role. The marginal probability for each component to hit 10 is highly sensitive to minutes and teammate availability; triple doubles are rare and dominated by high-assist bigs. Rules text defines the box score source and DNP treatment.
player_milestones.target: Player records a double-double or triple-double

interactions.hypothesis: Usage gain from teammate absence is strongest when the absent player shares position/role, and efficiency typically falls as usage rises.
Rim-attack scorers vs drop coverage and pull-up scorers vs switching have different expected efficiency than the team-level defense rating.
Foul-prone crews raise FTA for rim attackers; effect compounds with opponent foul rate.

When a co-star is out the scorer's usage rises but true shooting typically falls (harder shots, fewer assisted looks), so points rise by far less than usage; the loss is largest when the absent player is a primary creator whose assists generated the scorer's easy shots.

Blowout probability trims minutes only in the fourth-quarter tail, which removes the high-minutes branch where 30+ outcomes live; the 30+ rung is therefore several times more sensitive to blowout probability than the 15+ rung.

A drop-coverage defense raises expected points for a pull-up midrange scorer and lowers it for a roll finisher with the same usage; a switching defense does the opposite via mismatch creation, so scheme effects are conditional on shot type, not additive.

A player flagged questionable or just back from injury lives in a different minutes regime where the early-exit hazard rises several fold; the standard ladders refund only inactive players, so exits in the active state settle NO.

Two teammates' point totals in one game are not independent: a fast game lifts both counts together and a shared blowout trims both players' minutes together, while within a fixed possession pool a higher usage share for one lowers the other's, so the covariance changes sign with the regime and the joint tail of two ladder rungs differs from the product of the marginals.

player_points.label: NBA player points over/under ladder
player_points.mechanism: Points = minutes x (field-goal attempts per minute x points per attempt + FT contribution). The distribution is a mixture over minutes scenarios (normal, blowout-truncated, foul trouble, early exit) times an overdispersed attempts process. Teammate availability reallocates usage; opponent rim protection and scheme change shot quality; shooting luck is mostly noise to regress. The ladder structure and the sharp line already embed much of the average, so value concentrates in scenario weights, tails and stale prices after news.
player_points.target: Player points over a half-point strike at 10+, 15+, 20+ etc., with DNP handling per rules text

interactions.hypothesis: Rebounds scale with pool times minutes share; a fast, poor-shooting game lifts all rebounders.
Absence of a fellow big raises share more than minutes alone, but also increases foul and fatigue risk.
Opponent three-point-heavy profiles shift rebounds to perimeter players and away from bigs.
Bigs in foul trouble in lopsided games are most likely to see minutes truncated, creating fat left tails.

Expected rebounds equal minutes share times the pool times conversion share, so a fast game of poor shooting multiplies the benefit of a full minutes load; in a blowout the pool is large but the starter is on the bench, leaving the product small.

The share a big inherits when another big is absent depends on which player replaces the minutes: a stretch forward replacing a rim-runner gives the survivor extra share, a second center gives little; so the absence effect is conditional on the replacement type, not additive.

A team that crashes the offensive glass concedes transition chances and plays slower after its own misses; opponent transition frequency changes pace and the miss supply in subsequent possessions, so crash policy has a nonlinear effect on the pool via pace.

A big with a high foul rate in a lopsided game is likelier to be benched early in the first half and then not return, producing joint extreme left-tail minutes; the two sources of truncation are not independent because coaches avoid risking a foul-prone starter once the margin is large.

A designated or returning big carries a first-half-only appearance hazard; protected contracts refund this branch while standard contracts settle NO, so identical status information has opposite value in the two series.

For protected rebound contracts a halftime margin beyond about 20 points makes a no-second-half appearance likely for bench bigs but not for starters, so the refund branch probability and the value of the protection depend on the margin path and the player's rotation slot, in opposite directions for the two groups.

player_rebounds.label: NBA player rebounds over/under ladder
player_rebounds.mechanism: Rebounds = minutes x rebound chances per minute x conversion. Chances depend on the number of missed shots in the game (pace and both teams' shooting), where the player stands on the floor (rim vs perimeter), and share competition with other bigs. Opponent shot profile (3PA-heavy produces long rebounds), offensive rebounding strategy and teammate absences redistribute the pool. Blowouts cut starters' minutes and favor bench bigs.
player_rebounds.target: Player rebounds over a strike (typically 4+ to 14+)

interactions.hypothesis: Attempts per minute times minutes sets the attempts distribution; minute shortfalls matter more than make-rate drift.
Shrinkage weight depends on the number of career attempts; recent 3P% outlier only matters for low-volume shooters.
Losing a rim-pressure creator reduces open catch-and-shoot attempts against help-heavy schemes.
Opponent 3PA allowed matters mostly when the opponent's scheme is extreme; otherwise noise.

Expected threes are minutes times attempt rate times make probability, so minutes swings dominate for bench shooters whose attempt rate is high but whose minutes vary between 8 and 28; the same minutes error costs far more for a 9-attempt-per-36 shooter than a 3-attempt one.

The shrinkage weight on observed 3P% depends on cumulative attempts: a rookie with 150 attempts keeps little of a hot start while a veteran with 3000 attempts keeps most; recent form matters only for the low-attempt sample.

A shooter's loss from an absent creator equals the share of his assisted attempts that creator generated times the shortfall of replacements; the effect is therefore concentrated in specific pairs rather than being a general absence penalty, and shooters with diversified passers are insulated.

In a blowout the favorite's starters leave and bench shooters play expanded minutes with higher attempt rates, while the trailing team's shooters take more late threes; the sign of the effect of margin on threes depends on role, flipping between starters and bench specialists.

Team-level shooting shocks (a hot night for the whole team) correlate the made-three counts of teammates; this does not change marginals but matters for parlays or when the same team's shooters appear on several rungs at once.

player_threes.label: NBA player threes made over/under ladder
player_threes.mechanism: Threes made = attempts x make probability with attempts overdispersed and make probability shrunk heavily to talent; both vary with minutes, role, defensive pressure and shot openness. Opponent scheme (switch, drop, perimeter defense), pace and teammate absences determine attempt volume. Luck dominates make probability in one game, so the pregame edge is mostly in attempt volume and minutes rather than in 3P% trends.
player_threes.target: Player three-pointers made over a strike (1+ to 7+)

interactions.hypothesis: Team Q1 history is valid only if tonight's starting five matches; a changed starter makes it stale.
2H totals and margins depend on when starters sit, which depends on first-half margin and coach policy.
Opening-quarter pace differs from game pace and is team-specific; combine both teams' Q1 pace tendencies.
Periods exclude OT unless stated; a mismatch with game-level markets creates edges when books price with OT.

Team Q1 history is valid only if tonight's starting five matches the historical one; a changed starter makes the stored Q1 rating stale, and the loss is larger for first and third quarters than for second and fourth, where the bench pattern matters more.

Second-half lineups depend on the first-half margin: when the margin exceeds roughly 15 at halftime coaches shorten Q3 starter minutes and use bench units in Q4, so Q3 and Q4 are two different regimes whose scoring rates differ in both pace and efficiency.

Because 2H contracts include overtime and Q4 contracts do not, the 2H total is Q3 plus Q4 plus an overtime component with probability about 5-7% and size about 22-26 combined points (about 11-13 per team), producing a right-skew in the 2H total and a wedge to Q3+Q4 prices.

Tie probability and margin variance both rise as possessions per period fall because fewer scoring events produce smaller margins; slow-pace matchups therefore have higher tie mass and lower probability of crossing 7.5/8.5 margin strikes.

End-of-quarter fouling when the team is in the bonus produces clusters of free throws at near-100% value; this convexly raises Q4 totals when the game is within 5 points, whereas early-quarter fouls matter less because bonus onset is later.

quarter_and_half_markets.label: NBA quarter and half winner/spread/total/team total
quarter_and_half_markets.mechanism: Period scoring depends on lineups on the floor in that period (starters in Q1 and Q3, bench-heavy stretches in Q2 and Q4), period pace, and game state. Q1 is the most pregame-predictable (starters known), Q4 depends on score state and fouling. Period totals have wide relative variance, tie probability matters for winners, and the sum of period lines should reconcile with the game total.
quarter_and_half_markets.target: Quarter or half winner, margin, total or team total (OT excluded unless stated; ties possible)

interactions.hypothesis: Race-to-N thresholds below 15 depend almost entirely on starters and opening pace.
Points leader is a max over distributions; add variance from minutes tails, so favorites in blowouts lose leader probability to underdog stars.
First-possession advantage is worth little for N=20+ but matters for N=5-10.

Race thresholds below 15 depend almost entirely on the identity of the starters and the opening tempo; a starter swap changes the scoring-event mix per possession, and the effect is largest when the replaced player is the primary creator.

First possession is hypothesised to be worth about half a possession in points (unverified); in a race to 5-10 it is a large share of the total edge but for N of 25 or above it is swamped by rating gap and noise, so the effect shrinks like 1/sqrt(N).

When a co-star sits the top scorer's expected points rise and a rival for the leader title disappears, so the leader probability grows faster than the usage gain alone; the effect on the opposing team's best scorer is the opposite.

Overtime favors the highest-minutes stars while blowouts remove the favorite's stars; leader probability therefore switches between a star-dominated regime in close games and a bench-diluted regime in lopsided ones.

Negative same-team correlation in points lowers the chance of both teammates scoring high, so the maximum is often a single outlier; positive cross-team correlation via pace increases both sides' high tails, spreading leader probability across teams.

race_to_and_points_leader.label: NBA race-to-N and game points leader
race_to_and_points_leader.mechanism: Race-to-N is a first-passage problem on two scoring processes driven by early-game pace, efficiency and starters; ties of rate make home-court and first possession matter. Points leader selects the maximum of several players' point distributions across both teams: it depends on minutes, usage, efficiency, overtime, and blowout minutes loss, with ties handled per rules. Both are sensitive to the starting five.
race_to_and_points_leader.target: Which team reaches N points first; which player scores the most points in the game

interactions.hypothesis: Title and conference odds are convex in star availability; model the mixture rather than the mean rating.
Seed boundaries depend on tiebreakers and the regress-to-margin rating; teams over-performing point differential are overpriced.

Title and conference probability are convex in team strength and in star availability: a healthy-star scenario multiplies title odds several-fold while the injured scenario nearly eliminates it, so the correct estimate is a mixture over star-health states, not the rating at the mean health.

Seed and division contracts flip at exact ties; teams within one win of a cutoff have probabilities controlled by the tiebreak ledger (head-to-head, division record), which is a discontinuous rule on top of continuous win totals.

Early in the season the posterior is dominated by the prior; as games accumulate the weight shifts to results. The optimal weighting depends on roster continuity: teams with many new players update faster because the prior is less reliable.

Playoff rotation tightening raises star-heavy teams' strength in exactly the games that decide titles, so the bracket path matters differently for deep teams versus top-heavy ones; a bracket in which a deep team faces a star team early changes round probabilities beyond the rating difference.

A trade changes team strength and uncertainty with a lag of 10-20 games because the integration of a new player lowers early effectiveness; the rating update should widen variance at the time of the trade and then narrow.

Once a team is out of Play-In contention its incentive flips toward lottery position, and its late-season win probability drops below the rating-implied value; the worst-record contract is decided in this regime, so simulating the last 15-20 games with regular-season ratings overstates the weakest teams' wins.

Playoff qualification is near-certain for seeds 1-6, roughly 55-75% for seeds 7-8 and 20-35% for seeds 9-10 through the Play-In, and zero below; P(KXNBAPLAYOFF) is therefore a piecewise function of the simulated seed distribution with jumps at 6/7 and 10/11, while KXNBAPLAYIN is an indicator of seeds 7-10.

Two teams that meet three or four times have negatively dependent win totals, which raises the variance of their difference and lowers the chance of equal wins relative to independent draws; KXNBAH2HWINS and division titles both sit on that difference.

season_futures_team.label: NBA team season futures (title, conference, division, wins, playoffs, seed, round reach)
season_futures_team.mechanism: Probabilities come from a simulation: team ratings with uncertainty updated through the season, the remaining schedule with rest and home/away, injury scenarios for key players and the official tiebreaker/play-in structure; the playoffs add bracket path and series models with playoff-tightened rotations. Win-total and seed markets are sensitive to rating uncertainty and boundary effects; title odds are convex in star health. Market prices incorporate narratives; edges come from uncertainty handling, luck regression and rule boundaries.
season_futures_team.target: Team's season win total, seed, playoff/play-in qualification, round reached, conference/division/title

interactions.hypothesis: The probability of leading is a mixture over games played; the gap in totals matters less than who is likely to stay healthy.
Streak probability is the product of per-game thresholds; a small shortfall in minutes probability compounds over the streak.
Threshold rules create managed-absence incentives that change expected games played.

The probability of leading is a mixture over the number of games the candidate plays; a small current gap matters less than the chance that the leading player misses time, so leader probability falls faster than a gap-based normal calculation implies.

Applies only if a contract uses a minimum-games rule (none is sampled; KXNBASTATAVG waives it): then players near the threshold are managed to qualify, so expected games played is not independent of the rule and the leader probability steps at the threshold. Under KXNBASTATAVG the interaction collapses to a smooth average plus a mass at zero games.

A 20-game team streak (KXNBAWINSTREAK) or the league-longest streak needs roughly six weeks of near-certain wins, which in practice requires the team's stars to be healthy for the whole window; a single absence lowers per-game win probability for several games and usually ends the run, so the streak probability depends on the joint health of the top players over a window, not on the season-average rating.

For the longest-streak and last-undefeated contracts, a head-to-head meeting between two teams on runs (or two unbeaten teams) ends one of the runs with certainty, so their run lengths and first-loss days are negatively linked; simulating teams independently overstates the chance that two teams share the maximum streak (1/N payout) or are both still unbeaten past a given day.
A teammate's long-term injury switches the player's role regime for the rest of the season, changing the posterior mean and variance at once; to-date averages from the earlier regime are misleading.

A candidate's chance of being first to 50 falls with the number and early-season schedule of rival candidates, not only with his own tail: the same per-game exceedance gives a much lower race probability when three other scorers play more games in October and November, and same-day hits split the payout.

Total plus/minus is team net margin per minute times minutes played, so a strong team's starter accumulates margin quickly while a missed month cuts his total proportionally; the leader race is therefore a product of team strength and durability, and teammates are positively correlated through the team term.

A 325-point game is out of reach in regulation for almost all matchups and becomes possible mainly through one or more overtimes, each adding roughly 22-26 combined points; the season probability therefore scales with the multi-overtime probability of high-pace, evenly matched games rather than with average totals.

season_stat_markets.label: NBA season stat leaders, streaks, records and specials
season_stat_markets.mechanism: Players' season stat races and streaks depend on per-game rates, role stability, games played and thresholds, with injuries and rest as the main source of variance. Team record markets depend on game-level simulation. Streak markets (consecutive games meeting a threshold) depend on per-game hit probability and a persistence structure with absence risk. Rules define qualifying games and ties.
season_stat_markets.target: Season stat leader, player streaks, team records and special season outcomes

interactions.hypothesis: An injury to a key player during a series creates positive correlation across later games; independent-game models overstate the stronger team's sweep probability.
Playoff ratings should weight top-8 rotation; deep-bench teams lose their depth advantage.
Cup group tiebreakers on point differential create incentives to run up margins in some games and rest stars in others.

A star injury during a series makes later-game outcomes positively correlated, so independent-game models overstate sweep probability and the chance of an undefeated run; a healthy and an injured regime have different per-game probabilities and the lengths differ accordingly.

Group tiebreakers on point differential give incentives to run up scores in some games and rest stars in others; the value of margin is non-linear because it matters only if the team ends tied on record, and the probability of a tie depends on the state of the group.

Total home games is a convex function of advancement because deep runs add rounds each with up to four home games, while early exits produce few; the distribution is right-skewed and its mean is dominated by the probability of reaching the third and fourth rounds.

The pair probability is the product of two bracket-reach probabilities only after the groups are settled; before that, each team's path depends on which wildcard slots open, and a margin-driven tiebreak in one group can move a team into the other half of the bracket, changing which pairs are even possible.

Clinch-at-home depends on the venue sequence: under 2-2-1-1-1 a higher-seed winner clinches at home only in games 5 or 7, a lower-seed winner only in games 4 or 6, so the probability is a path functional; a larger home-court edge makes home teams win more of their games, which lengthens series between even teams (more 2-2 and 3-3 states) and shifts clinches toward the higher seed's games 5 and 7.

If teams facing elimination play above their rating and teams up 3-0 relax, series lengthen and 2+ game comebacks become more frequent than independent games imply; the effect exists only in specific series states, so it shifts the tails of the sequence distribution, not the winner.

A 40-point Finals margin is likelier in uneven matchups, which also end in fewer games, so the per-game tail and the number of games are negatively linked; treating them as independent overstates the blowout probability for lopsided Finals and understates it for even ones.

Second-round upset and sweep counts depend on which pairings survive round one: chalk first rounds produce even 1-4/2-3 matchups (few sweeps, few upsets by definition), while first-round upsets create mismatched or seed-inverted pairings, so round-two counts switch regime with round-one results.

series_and_cup.label: NBA playoff series winner/props and NBA Cup
series_and_cup.mechanism: A best-of-seven series is a sequence of correlated games with 2-2-1-1-1 home structure and playoff-tightened rotations; probability of winner and length derive from per-game win probability with state-dependent updating (injuries, adjustments) and correlation. Cup outcomes follow group tiebreakers (point differential), one wild card per conference and single-elimination games hosted by the higher seed through the semifinal, with a neutral final (2026-27: Hinkle Fieldhouse). Both require rule-accurate simulation and availability-aware ratings.
series_and_cup.target: Series winner, series length / sweep, and NBA Cup winner/stage outcomes

interactions.hypothesis: Rate times minutes gives mean; the 0.5 vs 1.5 rung sensitivity to dispersion is higher than to the mean.
Turnovers scale with touches; role change after teammate absence raises turnovers as ball handling load rises.
Blocks track opponent rim attempts more than total FGA; opponent shot profile is a stronger signal than pace.

Mean events equal rate times minutes, but rung probability at 2.5 or 3.5 is convex in the mean for a low-count process, so a small minutes increase raises the tail probability proportionally more than the mean; the effect is largest for a player whose mean sits near 1.

A rim protector who contests aggressively both blocks more and fouls more, so the same behaviour that raises block supply raises foul-trouble risk and minute loss; this makes blocks and minutes negatively dependent in the tail.

A blitz or full-court scheme raises opponent live-ball turnovers only against careless handlers; against a low-turnover primary handler the extra pressure yields deflections without steals, so the effect of scheme on steals is conditional on the opponent handler's turnover rate.

Official-scorer credit adds count noise and an arena-specific shift of a few percent of rate (both unverified), which matters most where the count distribution is dense near the threshold: a rate shift of a few percent moves P(3+) for a mean near 1 much more than for a mean near 0.3, so the effect is a mean shift whose impact depends on the distribution shape, not only extra dispersion.

The stocks sum has variance equal to the sum of variances plus twice the covariance; for versatile wings positive covariance raises the 4+ tail relative to independent components, while rim anchors have near-zero covariance.

Steals depend on opponent turnover-proneness and pace; blocks on opponent rim-attempt volume and own rim-protection role; turnovers on ball-handling load and pressure. Official-scorer credit is a notable noise source. Stocks sum correlated components.

Team strength is the minutes-weighted sum of player ratings, so the same rating matters more for a player with 28 expected minutes than one with 10; a top pick who is shut down removes both his rating and the minutes, producing a step in team strength rather than a gradual change.

Summer League totals are both higher-variance and higher-pace than regular-season; the variance of totals scales with possessions and with defensive looseness, so the sd of total and sd of margin move together with the format baseline.

A late announcement that a key rookie rests switches the team to a different regime (bench-heavy rotation, evaluation lineups); the market reaction depends on timing, and the same news before and after the order time has different value.

Importance and schedule density jointly determine who rests: on the second game of a back-to-back with no seeding stakes, minutes shift to bench and prospects, whereas the same schedule in a must-win game keeps starters; the effect of rest depends on stakes.

A candidate's MVP chance is roughly P(keeps playing) times P(chosen | plays through), so a top pick with the best per-game production can be a poor MVP bet if his team plans a two-game appearance, while a second-year player on a contending roster gains; the shutdown hazard multiplies the whole award probability.

interactions.hypothesis: Team scoring depends on offense/defense interaction in shot profile: rim-heavy offense vs rim-protecting defense differs from generic ratings.
The favorite's team total is shaded down by blowout probability and the underdog's up by late free throws; implied totals from linear spread/total miss this skew.
Own absence of a primary ball handler affects own pace, so both team points and total change.
Team-total, game-total and spread must cohere; incoherence signals a stale market.

Own efficiency against this defense depends on factor-level fit: a rim-heavy offense gains against a drop defense that concedes rim attempts, but loses against one that walls the paint; the additive rating difference averages these opposite cases and so errs systematically for extreme styles.

The favorite's expected points flatten when the game becomes lopsided because starters sit while the underdog's points keep rising through late fouls and bench scoring; the relation of team points to margin is piecewise with a kink around a 10-12 point expected margin.

A missing ball handler lowers both team efficiency and the possession count; the two effects multiply in the points total so a model that adjusts only the rating understates the points drop, and the opponent's points move too through the shared pace.

Trailing teams foul late and the leading team shoots the free throws, so crew foul tendency raises the favorite's points more in close games and the underdog's points via fouls drawn in garbage time; effect depends on the margin path.

A three-point-reliant team has high variance in points, so strikes far from the mean have probability much different from a low-variance team; luck regression (the three-point mean) and variance (the dispersion) are separate parameters that both matter for strike distance.

team_total.label: NBA team total points
team_total.mechanism: Team points = own possessions x own efficiency against the opponent's defense; dependent on the team's pace and on the game's margin (favorites' points reduced by garbage time, underdogs' points raised by late fouling). Injuries to the team's scorers and to the opponent's defenders move the team total directly; the market's team totals are derived from total and spread, leaving potential inconsistency across the three markets.

m.external_lines.label: Sportsbook / exchange reference prices with timestamps
m.external_lines.measurement: De-vig each book line (multiplicative or power), convert to implied mean/probability, track open-to-now movement and cross-book dispersion; compute Kalshi minus consensus per rung with staleness flags.
m.external_lines.mechanism: Sportsbook lines are an independent, highly liquid estimate of the same distribution and embed information (injuries, sharp money) that fundamentals miss.
m.external_lines.rationale: For NBA sides and totals the sharp closing line is hard to beat; for player props it is a strong prior on the mean and distribution. The informative quantity is the disagreement between Kalshi and the book after removing vig, and whether the book moved first. Subtle: timestamps must be point-in-time and props are often posted/stale at different times than main lines.

m.ladder_structure.label: Cross-rung consistency of the threshold ladder (monotonicity, implied distribution)
m.ladder_structure.measurement: Extract all rungs for the same player/stat/game, enforce monotonicity, difference to get implied P(X=k), fit mean and dispersion; flag rungs whose price is off the fitted curve by more than spread+fee; compute rung correlation for exposure netting.
m.ladder_structure.mechanism: A strike ladder is a set of tail probabilities of one underlying count; consistency across rungs exposes mispriced rungs and reveals the market's implied distribution.
m.ladder_structure.rationale: Over/under ladders (e.g. points 15+/20+/25+/30+) must be monotone non-increasing, and the implied pmf (differences between rungs) shows where the market puts mass. Rungs are heavily correlated, so a model edge on 25+ is largely the same bet as on 30+; position sizing must treat the ladder as one exposure. Also reveals integer-vs-half-point structure and whether the market's implied variance is wider or narrower than a count model.

m.orderbook_depth.label: Order-book depth and spread
m.orderbook_depth.measurement: Per rung: best bid/ask, size at best, cumulative size within 2c and 5c, spread in cents and as fraction of price; time-weighted averages over the last hour before tip.
m.orderbook_depth.mechanism: Depth and spread determine how much size can be filled at the quoted price and how large the round-trip cost is.
m.orderbook_depth.rationale: A mispricing smaller than the half-spread plus fee is not tradable. NBA player-prop rungs far from the main line are often wide and thin, so apparent edges there are frequently untradable. Depth also signals market-maker confidence: a quote that collapses in size near tip often precedes lineup news.

m.quote_history.mechanism: The market's own price path aggregates information (injury news, lineup confirmation, sharp flow) and defines the executable price at each decision time.
m.quote_history.rationale: Quote history is the only way to know what price was actually available at the decision timestamp, to measure line moves against injury-report vintages, and to separate stale quotes from real information. Subtle: last-trade prints on thin NBA prop rungs can be hours old, so mid-of-bid-ask with a staleness flag is safer than last price; and any model input must be joined point-in-time to a quote vintage, never to a closing price.

m.strike_hit_rates.mechanism: Empirical hit rates by rung reveal systematic miscalibration of the market in that family (favorite-longshot, over bias) independent of any fundamentals model.

Subtle: rungs on one game are correlated, so effective sample size is the number of games not markets, and hit rates must be conditioned on price bucket and line vintage.

nba.allnba_points_ladder.rationale: Candidates with similar profiles split votes and a margin of a few points moves a player between teams; ballots are positionless since 2023-24, so the old guard/forward/center constraints no longer bind and should not be modelled.

nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.label: All-Star exhibition effort, pace and score variance baseline, conditional on timed vs target format
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.measurement: Split all exhibition games by format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger. Timed games: points per team per minute, 3PA rate, margin SD per 12 minutes and late-compression coefficient (margin SD change over the final 4 minutes). Target games: points per possession for each team and possessions to reach the target, fed to nba.target_score_race_model. Shrink current-format estimates toward the pooled same-regime value (few games per format); as-of = last completed event; units = points and margin SD.
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.mechanism: Exhibition scoring and margin come from low defensive effort, extreme three-point volume and random clustering of makes; how effort evolves depends on whether the game is clock-timed (2026 All-Star Game: 12-minute games) or a race to a target score (Kalshi text for Rising Stars: first to 40 then 25). The 2025 format behind KXNBAALLSTAR is UNVERIFIED.
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.rationale: Margin variance is large relative to talent gaps, so short games raise the weaker roster's chance. In timed games effort rises in the final minutes and point differential can matter for the tiebreak; in target-score games the end is a race, so the two regimes must not be pooled, and margin SD must never be transferred between formats of different length (a 12-minute game is not a rescaled 48-minute game). The contract year fixes the regime: 2026 KXNBAALLSTARGAME is timed (rules text), KXNBARISINGSTARS is target (rules text); KXNBAALLSTAR 2025 has no format text and was not researched.

nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.label: All-Star Game team roster strength and composition
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.measurement: For each team sum over rostered players minutes_share_i * (0.6*OffImpact_i + 0.25*z(3PA per 36 * 3P%) + 0.15*z(AST%)), where OffImpact_i is multi-season offensive RAPM/EPM shrunk to 0 with prior weight 1,500 possessions; minutes_share from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan normalised to 1 (the three weights are fixed, not fitted). Output the team difference in impact-weighted points per 100 possessions. Converting it to an expected margin uses a scale factor that is FORMAT-SPECIFIC and is NOT fitted on pooled formats: timed 12-minute games (2026 round robin, one edition: scale UNVERIFIED, use a ridge prior centred on the per-possession rate times roughly 24 possessions per team per 12 minutes with wide uncertainty until more editions exist) and target-score races (margin is replaced by a per-possession edge fed to nba.target_score_race_model) are separate fits; long conventional All-Star Games (2013-2024 style) are only used to estimate the per-possession gap-to-margin relationship, never the margin scale for 12-minute games, and each format uses its own ridge penalty with the number of editions reported. Apply -0.5 point per missing big as a placeholder flagged UNVERIFIED. As-of = final roster after the replacement window; output every team pair.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.mechanism: The Game winner is the team whose assigned players are collectively better at scoring in an open-court, low-defence environment, built from impact, shooting and creation of the players who actually appear.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.rationale: Because the same selected stars are split among teams, gaps are small and dominated by composition: shooters and creators gain more than rim protectors in a low-defence game, and replacements change rosters late. In 2026 teams were built by nationality (USA Stars, USA Stripes, World), so one team can be systematically stronger, unlike a draft; the 2025 team construction behind KXNBAALLSTAR ('Shaq's OGs') was not researched here and is UNVERIFIED.

nba.assisted_three_passer_map.label: Share of shooter's made threes assisted by each teammate (passer dependence)
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.measurement: For shooter s over the last 2 seasons: share_sp = (made threes by s assisted by passer p + 40*q_p) / (made threes by s that were assisted + 40) where q_p is the team-average share of assisted threes from p, using play-by-play assist credit. Expected assisted-three makes lost = sum_p share_sp * P(p out) * (1 - r), where r is the replacement factor = (s three-point makes assisted per 36 in games p missed)/(same with p playing), shrunk to 0.65 with prior weight 5 games, clipped to [0,1]. Report the change in assisted-three makes per game (not attempts); as-of = injury-report vintage before tip.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.mechanism: A catch-and-shoot three requires a passer; the loss of a particular creator removes a specific fraction of assisted looks, with replacement playmakers delivering fewer.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.rationale: Absence adjustments built from with/without splits ignore that dependence is concentrated in a few passers; in many pairs one creator generates 30-40% of a shooter's threes, so his absence matters far more than other absences.

nba.implied_team_totals.label: Market-implied team points from spread and total
nba.implied_team_totals.measurement: implied_home = (T - S)/2 and implied_away = (T + S)/2 where S is home spread (negative = home favorite); deviation from the team's season average points; movement since open.

nba.implied_team_totals.rationale: Team implied total = (total ± spread)/2. Player props (points, assists, rebounds, threes) scale with team points and with the game's pace, and the implied totals move on injury news before box-score features update. It is the compact summary of the book's view of pace and offense in this exact matchup with current availability.

nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.label: League-wide probability of extreme single-game events over the remaining regular season (325+ combined points, 15+ steals plus blocks)

Steals plus blocks: per player-game, a bivariate negative binomial from shrunk per-36 rates (prior weight 1,000 minutes) times projected minutes, tail checked against 20 seasons of single-game maxima; P(any player >= 15) = 1 - product over player-games. Season probability = 1 - product over remaining games, Cup knockout games included and the Cup final excluded. As-of: nightly.

nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.rationale: These events sit far in the tail: a 325-point game needs exceptional pace and shooting and usually more than one overtime, and 15+ steals plus blocks by one player is extremely rare. Per-game probabilities are tiny and governed by tail shape (count of OT periods, heavy-tailed defensive activity), so fits to means can be wrong by orders of magnitude, and the union over about 1,230 games compounds the error.

nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.label: Distribution of the league-longest win streak and the number of tied teams (1/N payout) from game-level simulation

Step 3: per-team OT points = league points per team per OT period from play-by-play scaled by the team's opponent-adjusted pace and offensive rating relative to league; combined OT points = sum over both teams. Step 4: P(k-th OT | (k-1)-th OT) = pooled empirical tie rate of five-minute periods with prior weight 200 OT periods. Output P(OT), P(2+ OT), per-team and combined OT-points distributions. Subtle: the zero-margin mass is larger than a continuous normal approximation gives, because end-of-game tactics (holding for the last shot, fouling when ahead by three) cluster regulation margins between 0 and 3.

nba.pace.label: Pace/possessions, opponent-adjusted, lineup-aware

nba.pace.rationale: Pace is not additive: expected game pace is roughly league average plus each team's deviation, but slower teams usually win the tempo contest on defense and transition-heavy teams are constrained by opponent make-rates. Lineup changes (a primary ball-pusher out) shift pace. Blowouts and intentional fouling alter late possession counts.

nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.label: Probability a player reaches N points in at least one playoff game (union over a random, correlated run)
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.measurement: Simulate 20,000 playoff runs: draw the team's qualification and series path from the bracket simulation (nba.title_path, nba.series_length_distribution, nba.play_in_path_model), the player's availability per game from nba.playoff_star_health_hazard, a run-level form factor (log-normal, sd fitted from the player's game-to-game residual autocorrelation, about 0.1), and per-game p_g = P(points >= N) from nba.single_game_ceiling_tail rescaled by playoff minutes (nba.playoff_rotation) and opponent defender shift (nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift); P(YES) = share of runs with at least one game >= N. nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.mechanism: A playoff-long single-game threshold pays on the maximum game score over a random number of games whose length depends on advancement and the player's own health, with per-game tails correlated through form and matchup.
nba.playoff_any_game_threshold_union.rationale: Multiplying a regular-season per-game tail by expected games overstates the price: playoff pace and defense compress the tail, the number of games is zero with positive probability, health and advancement are linked, and a series against one elite defender correlates several games. nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.label: Distribution of the number of home playoff games by seed and path
nba.playoff_home_games_distribution.measurement: For each team and round compute P(reach round) and P(home-court | reach) from nba.title_path (better record hosts; Finals by record). nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.label: Playoff matchup assignment shift (primary defender effect)
nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.measurement: For each offensive player O and defender D in the same season compute points per 100 partial possessions guarded (matchup table, min 50 possessions), shrunk to D's overall defensive effect with k=100 possessions and to O's season rate. Shift = sum_D s_D x (shrunk matchup rate - O's baseline per-100 rate), reported in points and assists per 100, with a standard error from possession counts. Update after each series game with a 2-game half-life; as-of: games completed before tip. Treat the shift as noisy and cap its weight with an out-of-sample test.

nba.playoff_matchup_assignment_shift.rationale: Regular-season position-based opponent allowances miss the specific defender and the series adaptation. The 5-15% shift magnitude is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED (recalled, not estimated).

nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.label: Probability of winning a game after trailing by D or more points (max-deficit comeback rate)
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.measurement: From play-by-play for 15 seasons compute for each game the maximum deficit faced by the eventual winner, M. For each threshold D in {20,25,30,35} fit separately a logistic model P(M >= D) = f(own-model pregame margin mu, own-model margin sd, pace, playoff flag), pooling D by an ordinal-logit if counts are below 40 events, and shrink the playoff coefficient to the regular-season value with prior weight 200 playoff games. Output per-game P(winner trails by >= D) for each side as a function of mu. Series union = 1 - E[prod over games (1 - p_g)] using series length draws and the per-game mu; add a shared series random effect on the log-odds (variance estimated from playoff series) rather than assuming independence. As-of: before game 1 and after each game using realised results.
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.mechanism: A team wins after trailing by D only if the leader's in-game margin path reaches D and then reverses fully; large leads trigger starter rest and slower pace by the leader, so reversals from 30+ are rare and depend on when the lead was built.
nba.playoff_max_deficit_comeback_rate.rationale: KXNBASERIESGCOMEBACK settles on any series game won after a 30-point deficit, a path event that no final-score model sees: a game can end close after a 30-point swing. Both the chance of a 30-point lead and the chance of reversing it depend on the strength gap, pace and how coaches manage big leads in the playoffs.

nba.playoff_rotation.label: Playoff rotation tightening and minutes inflation
nba.playoff_rotation.measurement: For each player-season with >=20 regular-season games and a playoff series, compute the ratio r = playoff minutes per game / regular-season minutes per game (regular season through the last 20 games to avoid rest-game noise), pooled by role bucket (top-3 minutes, other starters, rotation, bench) and round, 2010-present, with shrinkage of player r to the bucket mean at k=8 playoff games. Team rotation depth = number of players averaging >=12 minutes in the series, versus regular season. Output for each player: expected playoff minutes = projected regular-season minutes x r_bucket,round with sd, conditioned on series pace and blowout probability from own-model margin. As-of: games before tip; regular-season baseline fixed at season end.
nba.playoff_rotation.mechanism: Playoff games feature shorter rotations and higher starter minutes, changing player props and team-level ratings relative to the regular season.
nba.playoff_rotation.rationale: Stars play several more minutes per game and bench depth matters less; regular-season minutes baselines understate playoff volume for starters and overstate bench contributions. Subtle: the effect varies by round and by series pace/blowout probability.

nba.playoff_star_health_hazard.rationale: Games-missed expectations average over a season; the quantity that matters for round-reach contracts is the probability of being healthy at tip of each playoff series, which depends on current injury state, history, age and minutes load.

nba.points_parity_band_mass.label: Composite points pmf with parity and free-throw effect for 2-point bands
nba.points_parity_band_mass.measurement: For each player draw attempts FGA2, FGA3, FTA from the nba.minutes distribution and per-minute attempt rates (negative binomial), then makes from beta-binomial with the player's shrunk rates and within-game dispersion from nba.within_game_make_dispersion; correlate FG2/FG3/FT counts through a Gaussian copula with correlations estimated on 5 seasons of player-games (pooled by archetype, shrunk with k=40 games). Points = 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FT. Tabulate P(points = k) on the integer lattice, check the mod-2 parity share against the historical frequency for similar players, and blend 0.8 simulated pmf + 0.2 smoothed empirical pmf of similar-usage players at the same projected minutes. Aggregate to the contest's band edges parsed from its rules text. As-of: games before tip, injury report vintage for minutes.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.mechanism: Points = 2 FG2 + 3 FG3 + FT; the mass of a 2-point band depends on parity coming from threes and free throws.
nba.points_parity_band_mass.rationale: Band probabilities from a smooth normal approximation ignore the lattice structure of the composite, which can misallocate up to several percentage points between adjacent bands.
