nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.label: Market-free prospect draft-slot probability model from public boards, measurables and team needs
nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.measurement: Step 1: consensus score = weighted mean of z-scored ranks across >=5 public boards and mocks (z within each board's top 60), weight = inverse of each source's mean absolute slot error over the last 5 drafts (equal weights if history is missing), plus a bonus for mocks published within 7 days. Step 2: Plackett-Luce over the remaining pool at each pick, theta_i = a x consensus_i + b x need_fit(team,i) + c x intl_or_age_flag(i). need_fit = 1 if the prospect's listed position is the position of the team's lowest minutes-weighted impact slot among its top-8 rotation players, else 0; flag = 1 if prospect is international or age >= 21 at draft. Fit a, b, c by maximum likelihood on the last 10 drafts. Step 3: simulate 20000 drafts with pick order from the lottery and ownership layers; output P(taken at or before slot k) and P(team picks within top k). No market price is an input. As-of: nightly in the final month, hourly on draft day; draft-night trades are separate scenarios.
nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.mechanism: Player-slot draft contracts (top 5, top 10, top 20 and so on) need the probability that a named prospect is selected at or before a slot, which is the product of the team's pick position (from the lottery and ownership layers) and a ranked-choice model of who each team takes.
nba.prospect_slot_probability_model.rationale: The catalog input nba.draft_board mixes a public consensus rank with 'the market may lead the public mocks', so it can smuggle a price into the model. A market-free version uses only non-price information: aggregated public big boards and mocks (weighted by their past accuracy), combine and workout measurables, age and team needs, and excludes any prediction-market or sportsbook draft price, which is kept as a benchmark only. Slot outcomes are strongly rank-ordered at the top and diffuse in the middle, so a ranked-choice model is needed and not a per-player independent probability.

nba.rare_make_accrual_rate.rationale: Non-shooters have an attempt rate that can change after an off-season shooting project; preseason attempts are the leading indicator, and the exposure window excludes playoffs and the Cup final.

nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.label: Ratings-based blowout probability and starter-minutes-vs-margin curve (market-free)
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.measurement: Step 1, expected margin: mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv, where NetRtg_adj is the as-of-tipoff opponent-adjusted net rating from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (ridge regression on game point differential, half-life about 25 games, shrunk to the preseason prior with n_prior about 20 games as a placeholder to be fitted), adjusted for the confirmed unavailable players via nba.lineup_adj_rating, home_adv fitted on the last 5 seasons (about 2 points). Step 2, margin spread: sd_margin fitted on 5 seasons of residuals of final margin versus mu (league-wide roughly 12-13 points, to be estimated, with a heavier empirical tail than normal). Step 3: P(final |margin| >= 15/20/25) and P(|lead| >= 15/20 entering Q4) from the empirical residual distribution around mu. Step 4, minutes curve: from play-by-play stints, per team-season, expected minutes of each rotation player conditional on margin entering Q4 in bins (0-9, 10-14, 15-19, 20+), shrunk toward the league curve with k about 30 blowout games. Output per player: expected minutes lost and the probability of falling below a stated minutes level. No closing line or other price is used; the spread is retained only to benchmark calibration of step 3.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.mechanism: Rebuilds the blowout risk from team strength and rotation history instead of the closing spread: a ratings-implied expected margin and margin spread give P(large lead), and a coach/player minutes-versus-margin curve converts each margin path into expected minutes lost by starters and gained by bench players.
nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve.rationale: The catalog input nba.garbage is defined from the closing spread, which is a market price and so a benchmark, not an input. The causal quantity is the chance that the margin passes the coach's pull threshold early enough to matter, and how much playing time each player then loses. Subtle: the loss depends on when the lead arrives (a 20-point lead entering Q4 removes far more starter minutes than one reached with 3 minutes left), on the coach, and on whether the trailing team also pulls starters, so the curve must be conditional on the margin path and not only on the final margin.

nba.rating_update_gain.label: In-season rating update gain and posterior sd (how fast current results override the prior)
nba.rating_update_gain.measurement: Backtest across the last 15 seasons: regress end-of-season margin per game on preseason prior and games-played-weighted current margin; solve for optimal weight w(n) as a function of games played n (expect w near 0.2 at n=10, 0.5 at n=40); posterior sd of true rating = sqrt(prior_var x (1-w)); use margin of victory capped at 15 and garbage-time excluded. As-of: all games before the as-of date.
nba.rating_update_gain.mechanism: True team strength is updated game by game with weight given by signal-to-noise; the gain declines with games played, and calibrating it by backtest sets how fast futures should move.
nba.rating_update_gain.rationale: A rating that overweights early results (10 games) swings futures; under-weighting leaves stale priors. The right gain is estimated from past seasons and depends on whether margin or win/loss is used and on roster stability.

nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.label: Own-model regulation tie probability P(OT)
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.measurement: P_gauss(0) = phi(mu/sigma)/sigma with mu own-model margin and sigma from own ratings and pace (nba.lineup_adj_rating and nba.pace; about 12, scaling with sqrt(possessions)); multiply by excess factor kappa(|mu|) estimated by isotonic regression on 10 seasons of games as observed OT rate divided by P_gauss(0) in |mu| buckets of 2 points; kappa about 1.7-1.9 overall; output with beta interval; use own-model mu, not closing lines. Margin is integer-valued with parity tied to the total, and free-throw, three-point and intentional-foul structure moves mass onto and off zero, so estimate the observed integer pmf at 0 (and smoothed mass at +/-1 to +/-4) over 15 seasons and let kappa(|mu|) absorb the discreteness rather than reading the continuous density at zero.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.mechanism: P(OT) = mass of regulation margin at zero from a heteroscedastic margin density with a late-game excess-mass correction.
nba.reg_tie_pmf_model.rationale: The draft claims P(OT) is roughly flat across spreads, but a Gaussian with sd 12 gives 3.3% at pick-em and 2.3% at 10 points, so the dependence on spread is large; the right model is a decreasing function with an empirical excess factor.

Subtle: effect sizes have shrunk in the sports-science era and must be fit on recent seasons only.

nba.return_timeline_hazard.label: Return-from-injury timeline hazard by injury type
nba.return_timeline_hazard.measurement: For each injury event 2015-present define t = days from the first public report date to first game appearance (right-censored at season end). Fit a Weibull survival model per injury category (ankle, knee, hamstring, back, foot/fracture, surgery, illness) with parameters shrunk to the pooled category with k=8 events, plus covariates: stated timeline (log days), team disclosure ratio (team's median actual/stated duration over its prior 10 events, shrunk to 1 with k=5) and age. P(return by T) = 1 - exp(-(t_T/scale)^shape) where t_T = days from the report date to T conditional on survival to the as-of day (use the conditional survival). Update at each new report; as-of timestamp = latest report vintage before the decision.
nba.return_timeline_hazard.mechanism: The probability a player has returned by a date follows a recovery time-to-event distribution with setbacks, not a point estimate.
nba.return_timeline_hazard.rationale: Reported timelines are lower bounds with setbacks; a return-by-date market is a CDF at a date, and the shape depends on the injury (ankle sprain versus stress fracture versus surgery).

nba.series_banked_points_state.label: Points already banked in completed series games (running team totals, running combined total and running differential)

Rung conversion: remaining requirement for the total is K_rem = K - B_total (P=1 if K_rem <= 0, otherwise tail probability of the remaining-games total under nba.series_sum_stopping_simulator started from the current series score); for the spread S_rem = S - D_team on the remaining-games differential. For the spread, a banked differential of +30 turns a 9.5 strike into a bet that the opponent outscores the leader by less than the remaining cushion. Using a series-start distribution after games are played would ignore this realised state.

Multiplying an expected length by an expected per-game total loses the multimodal shape (one mode per possible length) and the negative coupling between lopsided margins and short series, which is exactly where rung probabilities live.

nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.label: Shooting Stars team shooting skill and format conversion
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.measurement: FORMAT (verified from the official NBA rules PDF, sha256 ed035e65...b921): 4 teams x 3 players (2 NBA players + 1 NBA Legend); locations 1-7 in order = right-lane layup/dunk 2, 18-ft right baseline 2, right elbow 2, right-wing three 3, top of the key 2, left-corner three 3, long-range three 4; at locations 1-6 each player takes one shot in the team's declared order, at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a left-wing passer feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; clock = 1:10 per team per round; round 1 = all four teams, top two advance; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final; the higher final-round score wins (that round-1 scores do not otherwise carry is an inference from this wording, the PDF ignores them explicitly only in the first-round tiebreaker); first-round tiebreaker = tied teams rerun at 30 seconds, only that score counts; final tiebreaker = rerun for the full 1:10; a shot out of the declared player order does not count (and outside location 7 that player does not shoot again); a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts from a location or if it shoots from locations out of order. SCORE = 2*(correct-order makes at locations 1, 2, 3, 5) + 3*(makes at locations 4, 6) + 4*(makes at location 7). STILL UNKNOWN (PDF silent; carried as explicit labelled assumptions, never as facts): (U1) what a valid shot attempt is; (U2) what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement; (U3) whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full or only location 7; (U4) how many location-7 attempts each player completes inside 1:10 and whether the clock can run out before location 7 (EMPIRICAL_QUESTION); (U5) whether other editions use the same rules; (U6) Kalshi's treatment of ties, disqualification, replay and cancellation (u10b). Estimation: NBA players' P(make) at the right-wing three, left-corner three and long-range three from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile and at the 2-point locations from nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill; legend component: last five career seasons' 3P% and FT% with an age discount of 1.5 points of 3P% per year since retirement, shrunk to past legends' contest make rate with k = 50 shots, plus a shot-tempo term for the legend's attempts inside the clock; simulate 20,000 contests under the verified rules including the round-1 selection of two of four, with the tiebreak rules and a disqualification and out-of-order branch as labelled assumptions (size of the branch is empirical, not stated by the PDF), and report P(win). CONTRACT CONSTRAINT: KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS settles on which named team wins the contest; the 30-second rerun matters only when a tie decides the second final slot, the full 1:10 rerun only if the final ends level, and Kalshi's text has no tie, shoot-off, disqualification or team-change clause, so a tie is settled by whatever the league declares.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.mechanism: A Shooting Stars team (2026: four teams of two NBA players plus one NBA Legend; only Team Knicks of the four team names is franchise-named) scores by making shots from seven locations in order within a 1:10 clock; the team with the higher final-round score wins.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.rationale: Kalshi's KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS rules give only the team name and event date (rules_secondary is empty), so the format comes from the official NBA 2026 Kia Shooting Stars rules PDF (read directly 2026-11-09, sha256 ed035e65...b921; completeness/source_provenance/NBA_2026_Shooting_Stars.json): four teams of three (two NBA players plus one NBA Legend); seven locations shot in order 1 to 7 worth 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4 points (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, right-wing three, top of the key, left-corner three, long-range three); each player takes one shot at each of locations 1-6 in the team's declared shooting order and at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a designated passer at the left wing feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; 1:10 clock per team per round; the top two of four teams advance from round 1; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final and the higher final-round score wins; a tied round-1 result that decides advancement is rerun among the tied teams only at 30 seconds (round-1 scores ignored); a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10; a shot out of the declared player order does not count (and, other than at location 7, that player does not shoot again); a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts from a location or if it shoots from locations out of order. What stays unknown: how Kalshi applies those rules to settlement and, from the PDF itself, what counts as a valid shot attempt, what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement, whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full, and whether the two players must be current NBA players. Four of the seven locations (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, top of the key) are 2-point spots, so make rates there come from nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill and only the right-wing three, left-corner three and long-range three come from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile. A Legend is likely to have little or no current shooting data, so team skill mixes current rates for active players with older evidence; tempo matters as in the 3PT contest.

P(pts >= 54) = P(game >= 35) x GPD tail beyond 54 minus u; do not add a separate OT adjustment (already in the data); optionally condition on the opponent via own-model environment. P(at least one in remaining G games) = 1 - E[(1 - p)^G] with games-played uncertainty from nba.injury_risk_season; also store the season-to-date maximum (resolves YES if already met).
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.mechanism: A highest-scoring-performance contract is the maximum over about 70 games of a heavy-tailed scoring distribution, with extreme nights requiring high minutes, hot shooting, free throws and often overtime.
nba.single_game_ceiling_tail.rationale: The mean scoring rate is nearly irrelevant for 54+; the exceedance probability per game is a tail quantity that must be estimated with a peaks-over-threshold model and then compounded over remaining games (1 - (1-p)^G).

nba.single_game_margin_pmf.label: Market-free single-game margin distribution for Cup group games (ratings-implied mean, compressed tails)
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.measurement: For each remaining group game: mean margin mu = (NetRtg_home_adj - NetRtg_away_adj) * expected_possessions/100 + home_adv from nba.off_rtg and nba.def_rtg (opponent-adjusted, as-of tipoff); spread = empirical distribution of final-margin residuals (final margin minus mu) from the last 5 seasons of regular-season games, giving a pmf on integer margins with sd of about 12-13 points (to be estimated, not assumed); apply the blowout compression curve from nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve to the tail. Sum margins over a team's remaining group games by convolution and rank teams with the official tiebreak order. No closing line or other price is used.
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.mechanism: The Cup point-differential tiebreak needs the distribution of each remaining group game's final margin, which is a ratings-implied mean plus a spread that is compressed in blowouts when starters sit and widened by overtime-free tails.
nba.single_game_margin_pmf.rationale: The existing nba.score_resid is a residual against market lines, which is a book calibration, not an input. The tiebreak value of a margin depends on the raw margin pmf: a 20-point win counts the same in the tiebreak sum whether or not it was needed, but coaches ease off, so the margin tail is lighter than a normal distribution. The pmf is built from scores and ratings only.

Vintage rule: every team rating used (nba.off_rtg, nba.def_rtg, nba.lineup_adj_rating) must be the snapshot computed from games completed before that historical game's tipoff, stored daily over the 5 seasons, with the confirmed-inactive adjustment as of the pregame report; end-of-season or later-revised ratings are not allowed, as they leak the game's own result.

nba.team_points_margin_curve.rationale: Deriving team totals as (total ± spread)/2 assumes linearity; the empirical curve can differ by 1-2 points at large spreads, and this matters for strikes in a market keyed to the team's own points.

nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.label: Team-stat pair difference model (shared-pace correlation)

nba.team_stat_pair_difference_model.rationale: Treating the two teams' counts as independent overstates the sd of the difference and misprices the zero-tie mass.

nba.usage_allocation_model.label: Lineup-conditional shot-attempt allocation model for tonight's expected on-court unit
nba.usage_allocation_model.measurement: For each stint (2 seasons, 200-game half-life) the response is the vector of FGA + 0.44 FTA + TOV counts by the five on-court players. Model with a Dirichlet-multinomial whose logit-share is a ridge-regularised linear function of player creation archetype (on-ball minutes share), prior-season usage, and the count of other primary creators on the floor; estimate by marginal likelihood. Predict tonight's shares for each projected unit (weighted by expected minutes per unit from nba.minutes) and report the mean share and a standard error from the posterior. As-of: last injury report vintage and confirmed starters.
nba.usage_allocation_model.mechanism: Team attempts are a roughly fixed pie divided among the five on court according to creation roles, so a scorer's share is a function of the whole unit, not just whether one named teammate is out.
nba.usage_allocation_model.rationale: With/without splits rest on tiny samples and ignore that replacing a creator by a catch-and-shoot wing shifts shots differently than replacing him by another creator; an allocation model with role types generalises across rosters.

nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.label: Within-team scoring allocation dependence
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.measurement: For each team and pair of top-6 players, compute the correlation of player points conditional on team points (partial correlation) using 3 seasons of games, shrunk to the role-pair prior with k=40 games; combine with team total correlation to get unconditional pairwise correlations; separate regimes with/without a major teammate absence.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.mechanism: Teammates split a fixed team total, giving negative dependence between teammates' counts conditional on team points.
nba.within_team_allocation_dependence.rationale: Treating two teammates' overs as positively dependent through the team total omits the allocation effect that offsets it at fixed pace; the net sign depends on how much variation in the team total versus in the split drives each leg.

inputs.why: Format vector per event-year (game length or target, number of teams, pairing rule, round-robin tiebreak order, roster rule) so every historical label joins to its own format and unverified fields stay flagged.
Exhibition margin variance and late effort set how much of a talent gap converts to a win, separately for timed 12-minute games and untimed races.
Who plays and how many minutes in each game of the format, including fatigue over a second or third game, changes the effective roster.
Round-robin pairing, point-differential tiebreak and bracket simulation turn pairwise team gaps into champion probabilities.
Selection, captains and participation determine who is eligible for each roster and each event.
Reserve selection and injury replacement set roster membership that feeds roster strength.
Offensive impact ratings feed the roster composite; defensive components are discounted because exhibition defence is minimal.
Injury reports before the weekend drive withdrawals, replacements and reduced minutes across all three events.
Announcements of rosters, captains, drafts and format arrive as news before official lists.
Format changes announced by the league (game length, scoring targets, pairing) alter the model for the next edition.
Announcement timing of rosters, drafts and format sets the as-of date for every input.
Rules fix the 12-minute round robin, the 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak, the 40/25 targets and show where the text is silent.
Official champion announcements are the labels and need reconciling with the contract source.
Team strength of the actual All-Star rosters (nationality-built in 2026; the 2025 construction is UNVERIFIED) in a low-defence exhibition is the core input of every exhibition series.
Rising Stars (quoted 40/25 targets, KXNBARISINGSTARS) is a race, so its winner requires this model; any 2025 All-Star race format is UNVERIFIED and not assumed, and a clock rule is unstated.
Rising Stars teams (KXNBARISINGSTARS only) of first/second-year and G League players need their own shrunk, cross-league strength rating.
The 2026 nationality split (KXNBAALLSTARGAME only; at least 16 US and 8 international players, Commissioner additions) decides how deep the World team is against the two US teams.
Three-point volume shapes roster scoring in a high-3PA exhibition; context for the 2026 All-Star Game rosters only.

interactions.hypothesis: Win probability is the roster gap divided by the margin standard deviation, and that deviation is set by game length and late effort, so one and the same gap yields a smaller edge in a 12-minute game than in a 48-minute one and a different edge in a race to 25.

In the three-team round robin a team needs margin only when all three finish 1-1; otherwise wins alone seed the final. A deep team's value therefore switches from win probability to expected point differential in the 1-1-1 branch, and the team that sits out Game 1 plays both remaining games against opponents who have already played.

A per-possession edge converts to a win concavely in a race to a small target because few possessions are played; the same Rising Stars roster edge yields a larger win probability in the 40-point semifinal than in the 25-point final, as the 2026 final finished 25-24.

A star with a minor injury often plays sharply reduced minutes or none, so the loss to team strength is a threshold at the status tier, not a gradual decline; in a 12-minute game one skipped shift is a large share of his total.

With teams built by nationality, the World roster is drawn from a much smaller pool than the two US rosters, so its depth and top-end talent depend on how many internationals the Commissioner adds and on who withdraws; the same star withdrawal costs World more than a US side.

A team that plays three games (Stars and Stripes in 2026) spends minutes across them, while World played two; late-bracket fatigue and coach minute-sharing change effective strength in the championship game, so the conditional strength of a finalist is not its round-one strength.

all_star_exhibition_games.label: NBA All-Star exhibition games and Rising Stars tournament winners
all_star_exhibition_games.mechanism: An All-Star exhibition champion comes from selected or drafted rosters (a nationality split with Commissioner additions in 2026, coach drafts for Rising Stars), the minutes and effort of the players who appear in games of only 12 minutes or races to 40 and 25, a single-game conversion with large variance, and a tournament structure (Game-1-dependent pairings, point-differential tiebreak, seeding to a final) that turns single games into a champion. Inputs are scoped per series (KXNBAALLSTARGAME: nationality quota, roster composite, path simulation; KXNBARISINGSTARS: Rising Stars rating and race model; KXNBAALLSTAR: roster composite and path simulation only, its 2025 format being UNVERIFIED) because the formats differ.

inputs.why: The MVP is the combined panel-and-fan outcome conditional on which team wins; this model is P(champion) times the panel's choice among that team's players plus a residual for a non-champion winner.
Carries the in-game fan ballot (reported as 25% of the decision in 2026) as a separate component from the panel and from the January starter vote.
Champion and finalist probabilities per team come from the tournament simulation, and MVP probability is capped by the player's team path.
Minutes inside capped 12-minute games bound how many points and moments a player can accumulate across the tournament.
Home-market, farewell and storyline effects shift the panel and fan choice among comparable stat lines.
Shot share inside the exhibition decides who posts the standout line, and it is the best pregame proxy for who will take the shots.
Team strength feeds P(champion) and the share of the scoring pool available to each player.
The exhibition scoring baseline and variance decide how large the top individual line can be in a timed game.
Injury status before the game drives both participation and minutes, which cap a candidate's chance.
Announcements of rosters, replacements and the voting process arrive as news before official lists.
Records the MVP selection method, panel and fan weights and whether the award covers the whole tournament or the final, each with its provenance flag.
Announcement timing of rosters and the voting method sets the as-of date for every input.
Changes to the format or the MVP process announced by the league alter the conditional structure of the award.
The rules fix withdrawal-to-No and show that the selection method, co-MVP handling and source are not stated.
The official MVP announcement is the label and must be reconciled with the contract source.
The MVP market resolves to No for a selectee who does not participate, so P(participates) for All-Star selectees (not contest entrants) multiplies every Yes price.
Regular-season production is only a context prior for an exhibition MVP; its odds and media-consensus narrative proxies are market-derived and are not used.
Offensive impact is context for team strength through the roster composite; it does not drive the exhibition MVP vote.

interactions.hypothesis: P(MVP) is roughly P(player's team wins the tournament) times his conditional share of the vote, with a residual for a non-champion winner; a dominant scorer on an underdog team stays priced low while a moderate scorer on the heavy favourite rises, and in a three-team round robin the runner-up's best player can still draw votes.

If fans carry a quarter of the decision and the panel carries the rest, a player with a modest panel share but a large fan share can overtake a panel favourite whenever the panel splits; the 2026 panel reportedly split 10-4 between two players, so the fan component matters most when the panel is split.

A star's contribution is capped by the shared minutes and shot pool: once he plays the full allowed minutes and takes the bulk of the team's attempts, extra usage cannot raise his line, so a higher regular-season usage helps less than linearly in a minute-shared exhibition.

Because non-participation resolves to No, a status downgrade from probable to doubtful removes most of a candidate's Yes value at once, and a late injury replacement creates a new candidate whose MVP probability is small but nonzero.

Fans can only vote for what they see: a player who plays the allowed minutes in all three games has three games of visible moments, while a star who plays one short game or sits the final has few, so the fan component's reach depends on minutes and appearances (a measurable variable), not on a general narrative.

Difficulty beats polish only when the panel's top-score compression is low; with lenient panels a clean easy dunk ties a hard one.
Entrant injury status shifts both his own winning chance and the rest of the field through the replacement draw.

Win probability is a max-of-noisy-scores function of per-ball make rates, so a shooter's gain from a few points of make probability is bigger when the field is thin at the top and shrinks as more strong shooters enter.

Judged score saturates near the scale maximum, so extra difficulty adds little once a clean dunk already earns near-perfect marks, while a miss subtracts a lot; this reverses the naive hard-dunk advantage.
A withdrawal changes the winner probability differently depending on the number of finalists and rounds: with fewer rounds a replacement has a larger chance to win through variance.

The gain from placing the all-money rack at a shooter's best location depends on the ball values and whether deep bonus balls exist in that year's format; a large location split is worth more when money balls carry double value and less when deep balls dominate the maximum.

With the verified spot values (2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4), a make at the long-range last spot (location 7) is worth twice a layup and location 7 allows ordered attempts until the clock expires while locations 1-6 give each player one attempt, so a team's expected score depends on the NBA players' and the legend's long-range rate and on how many location-7 attempts remain after the first six locations; a legend with a poor long-range rate is cheap at the layup spot but, because players shoot in declared order at location 7, still costs attempts there, so team skill is a lineup-and-spot assignment, not a team average. Which player takes how many location-7 attempts inside 1:10 is an empirical question.

The Shooting Stars winner needs a top-two round-1 score and then a higher final score, so the favourite's advantage is compounded over two noisy draws and the final can be won by a team that was only second in round one. The league PDF states the tie regimes: a round-1 tie that decides advancement is rerun at 30 seconds among the tied teams only (round-1 scores ignored) and a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10, so the tiebreaker rewards different skills (a 30-second clock weights the one-shot locations over location 7); how Kalshi settles a tie is not stated, so the tie regime is its own branch.

The layup/dunk spot is close to certain for most current athletes, so on that spot the difference between teams is seconds per attempt, while on the baseline, elbow and top-of-key spots a legend's mid-range touch decides whether he costs the team points; the team total therefore depends on tempo at the rim spot and on the legend's mid-range rate, neither of which a three-point profile reveals.

all_star_weekend_events.label: NBA All-Star Weekend skills contests (3-point, slam dunk, Shooting Stars)
all_star_weekend_events.mechanism: Each series settles on the winner of a one-off skills contest: the league invites the field and a withdrawn named player resolves No (3PT, dunk); performance is timed rack shooting with no defender, judged dunks with a miss risk, or a three-player team (two current players and a legend) shooting from seven fixed spots against a 70-second clock; the format turns performance into a winner through rounds, advancement cuts, a final that resets scores and tie procedures. Winners are maxima over a few noisy scores, so favourites are capped and format parameters matter as much as skill. Inputs are scoped per series because the three processes are disjoint.
all_star_weekend_events.target: Winner of an All-Star Weekend skills contest: the 3-Point Contest, the Slam Dunk Contest or the Shooting Stars team contest

interactions.hypothesis: Series total is length times per-game total, so sensitivity of a rung to the per-game total is highest near a length mode and lower, though not zero, between modes.
The stopping rule couples per-game margins and series length, so expected cumulative differential grows concavely with the rating gap.
A mid-series star absence switches the path regime, moving margins, win probability and series length together.
Playoff pace and whistle shifts apply to every game and add to the shared series factor, so they move the whole total distribution rather than averaging out.

Within the simulator the series total is about simulated length times per-game total (length drawn jointly, not from the separate DP pmf), so a 5-point shift in per-game total moves a 4-game sum by 20 and a 7-game sum by 35; a rung at a mode centre is highly sensitive to per-game total while a rung in a trough is less sensitive, by an amount that depends on the within-mode sd (about 40-65 points).

Margins decide game wins, so large positive margins for one side shorten the series; the cumulative differential and length are negatively dependent, and treating them as independent overstates the differential in lopsided matchups and understates its spread in even ones.

Losing a star mid-series shifts every remaining game's margin by several points and the win probability with it; this can lengthen a series the injured team was winning or shorten one it was losing, moving total and differential at once.

The decisive game's margin regime depends on series state: a team trailing 0-3 may concede late and lose big, while game-7 margins compress; because the decisive game always counts, this changes differential tails asymmetrically.

Fewer possessions and fewer free throws per possession multiply into lower per-game points, and since both apply to every game they add to the series-level factor, shifting the whole total mixture down rather than averaging out across games.

Large leads shrink once starters sit, so each game's contribution to a dominant team's differential saturates; combined with fewer games in lopsided series, the cumulative differential grows much slower than the rating gap at the top end.

Once banked points approach the strike, the rung reduces to whether one more or two more games are played, so probability switches from a smooth tail to a length bet; when the banked sum already exceeds the strike the total is certain, a hard threshold in the remaining requirement K - B.

series_cumulative_points.label: NBA playoff series cumulative team points (total and spread)
series_cumulative_points.mechanism: Both contracts sum per-game quantities over a best-of-seven series that stops when one team reaches four wins. The total is approximately series length times a playoff-adjusted per-game total, so its distribution has one mode per possible length (4-7 games) and rungs between modes largely price length. The differential sums game margins; margins also decide who wins each game, so the stopping rule couples them: lopsided series end quickly and accumulate a large differential in few games, while even series run long with margins that partly cancel. A shared matchup regime correlates games, mid-series injuries switch paths, close-out games and blowout truncation shape the decisive margin, and whether overtime counts is not stated in the rules.
series_cumulative_points.target: Combined points or cumulative point differential of two teams summed over all games of a playoff series vs a strike

contract_types: Any player scores 50+ points in a playoff game

interactions.hypothesis: Usage matters only with minutes; the product drives all components together.

The contract compounds a small per-game tail over a random number of games; for p near 1% the value is roughly p times expected games, so a contender's star with 18 expected games is worth several times an equal scorer on a first-round team.

Advancement is conditional on the star's health and his games are conditional on advancement, so the joint probability of 'healthy and still playing in round three' exceeds the product of marginals for teams that depend on him and falls below it for deep teams.
Playoff minutes inflation applies only in competitive games; in a lopsided series the star sits fourth quarters, so the heavy-minutes regime needed for 50 depends on the series strength gap.
When a co-star is out, usage jumps by several points and the 50-point tail thickens sharply; with both creators healthy the tail is thin, so the effect is a regime switch rather than a linear shift.

An elite primary defender assigned for a whole series lowers the scale of the tail for every game of that series, so the per-game tails are positively correlated within a series and the union is smaller than independent games imply.

team_and_player_counting_specials.label: NBA playoff single-game scoring milestone (any player 50+ points in any playoff game; union over the playoff games)
team_and_player_counting_specials.mechanism: A player reaches 50+ points in at least one playoff game: the probability is a union over a random number of playoff games of a single-game upper-tail event, driven by the team's playoff path (games available), the star's availability and playoff minutes and usage, and the scoring tail against playoff defenses; cumulative points across games do not count.
team_and_player_counting_specials.target: Whether at least one player scores 50 or more points in at least one game of the playoffs (a union event over a random number of games and players).
